SECTION 2 - DEFINITIONS AND IN-PATIENT BENEFITS

2.1 In-patient Care means treatment for which the Insured Person has been admitted to a Hospital for a minimum period of 24 consecutive hours for the sole purpose of availing medical treatment. This condition shall not apply to Day Care Treatment.

2.2 Hospital means any institution for in-patient and day care treatment registered under the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, or which satisfies all of the following criteria: (a) has qualified nursing staff under its employment round the clock; (b) has at least 10 in-patient beds in towns having a population of less than 10,00,000 and at least 15 in-patient beds in all other places; (c) has qualified medical practitioner(s) in charge round the clock; (d) has its own fully equipped operation theatre; and (e) maintains daily records of patients.

2.3 Medically Necessary Treatment means treatment which is required for the medical management of the illness or injury, has been prescribed by a Medical Practitioner and does not exceed the level of care necessary. A hospital admission primarily for diagnostic or evaluation purposes is not Medically Necessary Treatment.

2.4 In case of an Accident, the Insured Person shall furnish the First Information Report and the Medico-Legal Certificate wherever applicable.

3.1 In-patient Hospitalisation. The Company shall pay Medical Expenses for Room, Boarding and Nursing; Intensive Care Unit; Surgeon, Anaesthetist and Specialist fees; operation theatre charges; medicines and drugs; diagnostic procedures; blood and oxygen.

3.2 Day Care Treatment. The Company shall pay Medical Expenses for the Day Care procedures listed in Annexure I, which contains 612 day care procedures, and for any other day care procedure that meets the definition of Day Care Treatment.

3.3 Pre-hospitalisation and Post-hospitalisation. These expenses are payable provided that a claim has been admitted under In-patient Care or Day Care Treatment and the expenses relate to the same condition for which the claim was admitted.

3.4 Domiciliary Hospitalisation means medical treatment taken at home which would otherwise require hospitalisation because the Insured Person is not in a condition to be removed to a Hospital or because of non-availability of a room in a Hospital, and which continues for at least 3 consecutive days. The following are not covered under Domiciliary Hospitalisation: asthma, bronchitis, chronic nephritis, diarrhoea, diabetes, epilepsy, hypertension, influenza, tonsillitis, arthritis, gout and rheumatism.
=== PAGE BREAK ===
SECTION 3 - ADDITIONAL BENEFITS

3.5 Maternity Benefit. The Company shall pay expenses for delivery, including a caesarean section, of a child by Asha Verma only. This benefit is available for a maximum of 2 deliveries during the lifetime of cover under the Master Policy. Lawful medical termination of pregnancy and treatment of ectopic pregnancy are included; complications of pregnancy requiring hospitalisation are covered. Pre-natal and post-natal expenses are payable only when incurred during the delivery hospitalisation. A New Born Baby is covered from day one for treatment within the maternity limit.

3.6 Chronic Care Programme. Insured Persons diagnosed with diabetes or hypertension may enrol in the Chronic Care Programme under which consultations, scheduled investigations and medicines for chronic disease management are covered from day 1, including pre-existing diseases covered from enrolment.

3.7 High-cost treatments. Dialysis, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, organ transplant and cardiac procedures are covered as In-patient Care or Day Care Treatment.

3.8 Modern Treatment Methods. Oral Chemotherapy, Immunotherapy, Robotic surgeries and Stem cell therapy are covered either as In-patient Care or as part of Day Care Treatment. Stem cell therapy is covered only for haematological conditions.

3.9 Organ Donor Expenses. The Company shall pay the in-patient expenses of the organ donor for harvesting of the organ donated to the Insured Person, when the recipient's transplant claim is admissible. Pre-operative and post-operative donor care is not payable.

3.10 Bariatric Surgery. Bariatric surgery is covered only when the Insured Person is aged 18 years or above, has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 40 or more, or a BMI of 35 or more with co-morbidities, has failed less invasive methods of weight loss, and the surgery is prescribed by a Medical Practitioner.

3.11 Mental Illness. In-patient treatment of Mental Illness is covered when taken in a hospital registered under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, on the advice of a psychiatrist.

3.12 Home Care Treatment. Treatment at home is covered with prior approval of the TPA, where the Medical Practitioner advises it in writing and daily monitoring records are maintained.

3.13 Rehabilitation. In-patient rehabilitation and physiotherapy after discharge following stroke or major surgery are covered when prescribed by a Medical Practitioner.

3.14 AYUSH Treatment. In-patient treatment under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy is covered only when the treatment is taken in an AYUSH Hospital. Treatment at a wellness centre, spa or resort is not covered.

3.15 Dental and vision. Dental treatment and spectacles are payable only when necessitated by an Accident requiring hospitalisation.

3.16 Wellness Programme. Insured Persons earn wellness points under the Wellness Program for completing annual health activities. Points accumulated can be redeemed as a discount on renewal premium of the conversion policy.

3.17 Health Check-up. A preventive Health Check-up is covered once at every renewal for an Insured Person aged 18 years or above after two continuous claim-free Policy Years, at a network diagnostic centre.

3.18 Vaccination. Anti-rabies vaccination following an animal bite (post-bite) is covered.

3.19 Second Medical Opinion. A second opinion (e-opinion) from a panel specialist is covered for any diagnosis of a listed Critical Illness.

3.20 Critical Illness Benefit. A lump sum is payable on first diagnosis of cancer, heart attack or stroke, provided the Insured Person survives for 30 days after first diagnosis (survival period). The benefit is in addition to the indemnity benefit.

3.21 Hospital Daily Cash. A fixed Hospital Daily Cash is payable per day of hospitalisation after an in-patient stay of more than 48 hours, with the first 24 hours not payable, for a maximum of 10 days per Policy Year.

3.22 Treatment outside India. Planned treatment abroad is covered only for the listed Critical Illnesses, where the illness is diagnosed in India, with prior approval of the Company, converted at the rate of exchange on the date of payment. Treatment in the USA and Canada is not covered. Territorial Scope: worldwide excluding USA and Canada.

3.23 Tele-consultation. Virtual consultation with a medical practitioner through the mobile application of the TPA is covered.
